question: Characterise the 111% single-chart CPU ceiling at 60x. Fourth assignment, previously zero commits.
verdict: REPRODUCED on the deployed product and attributed. 134-140% of a core, of which the main thread is 74-76% and 60-64 percentage points are off the main thread. The claim is real and it is NOT main-thread JavaScript alone — which is why every prior callback probe read ~7% and missed it.
surface: deployed http://31.97.192.82:3000, dist-v9 shell, single panel (mcLayout=1), replay playing at 60x, 2011 bars

instrument.method: CDP Tracing over devtools.timeline + toplevel + blink + cc + gpu for a 10s window; per-thread busy time is the UNION of event intervals so nested slices cannot be double counted; the total is deliberately allowed to exceed one core.

instrumentCorrection.problem: The first live reading was 266% because GpuVSyncThread emits ONE trace slice covering the entire window. That slice is a block on vsync, not CPU, and by interval-coverage it looks like 100% of a core.
instrumentCorrection.fix: Threads are excluded from the total only by documented name (GpuVSyncThread, Chrome_IOThread, MemoryInfra), and every exclusion is reported in `waitDominatedThreads` so it is auditable.
instrumentCorrection.whyNotAHeuristic: I first excluded any thread whose busy time was a single window-spanning run. That rule would silently discard one enormous main-thread task, which is the exact pathology this census exists to catch. Such threads are now FLAGGED (`singleRunSpansWindow`) and still counted; a unit test pins that behaviour.

whyPriorProbesRead7Percent: The existing PO-CPU profile samples main-thread scheduled callbacks on the hermetic harness. Two structural misses: it never drove the deployed product (74% of a core there), and 61 percentage points of the cost is off the main thread, where a callback probe cannot see it by construction.
supersedes: W75's attribution of this ceiling to m20Q6InertableScheduledCallback, retracted in W76 as an instrumentation wrapper artefact. This packet replaces it with a per-thread measurement.

idleFloor.note: Same instrument, chart loaded, replay NOT started (--idle).
idleFloor.readingForP4: The PO's idle floor of ~7.79% is the same order as the 10.17% main-thread figure here. A's ablation (13.12% measured, 6.3pp instrument, 0.17% React pumps) only ever examined the main thread, and 12.51pp of the idle cost is off it — over half. That is where the unexplained remainder should be looked for. Not closed; located.
idleFloor.instrumentOverheadCaveat: Tracing is active during these readings; StackSamplingProfiler at 0.28% is mine, and trace machinery inflates the thread-pool rows somewhat. Treat idle numbers as an upper bound.
